title: "GC processing test for NACME derivatized amino acids"
output: html_document
date: "2026-10-07"

```{r setup}
experiment_config_relative <- file.path(
  "data", "202609_tp_AAs_GC-IRMS", "experiment_config.yaml"
)
project_root_candidates <- c(".", "..", "../..", "../../..")
project_root_matches <- project_root_candidates[vapply(
  project_root_candidates,
  function(root) file.exists(file.path(root, experiment_config_relative)),
  logical(1)
)]

if (length(project_root_matches) == 0) {
  stop("Could not locate the AA experiment config from the current directory.")
}

project_root <- project_root_matches[[1]]
config_path <- file.path(project_root, experiment_config_relative)
lab_config_dir <- file.path(project_root, "..", "sessions_lab_isotidy_config")
gc_methods_path <- normalizePath(
  file.path(lab_config_dir, "gc_methods.yml"),
  winslash = "/",
  mustWork = TRUE
)
config <- load_IRMS_config(config_path, lab_config_dir)
raw_gc <- load_gc_data(config)
external_standard_id <- "F8"
aa_mix_sample_id <- "AA" # Override if the AA mix uses another export label.

# Imported rows should be unique across all instrument fields, even when an
# observation was present in more than one overlapping export.
stopifnot("source_file" %in% names(raw_gc))
stopifnot(nrow(raw_gc) > 0)
imported_source_files <- unique(unlist(strsplit(
  raw_gc$source_file,
  "; ",
  fixed = TRUE
)))
gc_yaml <- yaml::read_yaml(config_path)$gc
gc_selected_input_set <- gc_yaml$input_sets[[gc_yaml$selected_input_set]]
stopifnot(all(grepl(
  gc_selected_input_set$file_pattern,
  unique(raw_gc$source_file),
  ignore.case = TRUE
)))
gc_observation_fields <- setdiff(names(raw_gc), "source_file")
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(raw_gc[, gc_observation_fields, drop = FALSE]))
stopifnot(all(!is.na(raw_gc$source_file) & nzchar(raw_gc$source_file)))
```

## Assign each injection with its recorded GC method

The adapter uses the `ConFlo Method` value on each injection, so F8 runs use
`YP_CO2_F8_27m` and amino-acid runs use `YP_C_AA_59m`. Do not force one method
for the entire mixed input set.

## Process GC peaks through external-standard and NACME correction

```{r process-gc}
gc_result <- process_gc(
  raw_df = raw_gc,
  config = config,
  gc_methods = gc_methods_path,
  external_standard_id = external_standard_id,
  derivatization_sample_id = aa_mix_sample_id,
  isotope = "C13",
  verbose = TRUE
)

gc_result$daily_offsets
stopifnot(is.data.frame(gc_result$visualization_data))
stopifnot("delta_value_final_mean" %in% names(gc_result$visualization_data))
stopifnot("delta_value_final_sd" %in% names(gc_result$visualization_data))
stopifnot(nrow(gc_result$derivatization_estimates) > 0)
stopifnot(!any(gc_result$output$is_derivatization_standard))
gc_result$derivatization_estimates
```

## Review compound assignment

Unmatched and ambiguous peaks remain unassigned for review.

```{r compound-assignment-summary}
gc_assignment_summary <- gc_result$data |>
  dplyr::count(compound_match_status, compound_id, name = "n_peaks")
gc_assignment_summary
```

```{r f8-assignments}
f8_assignments <- gc_result$data |>
  dplyr::filter(sample_id == external_standard_id) |>
  dplyr::count(injection_id, compound_id, compound_match_status,
               name = "n_peaks") |>
  dplyr::arrange(injection_id, compound_id)
f8_assignments
```

## NACME correction target

The correction starts from F8 externally corrected values. For each compound and
calendar date, use the configured AA mix standard injections (the standard is
listed as `AA` in the standards configuration; the synthetic workbook labels its
runs `STD`) to calculate the mean derivative value and its injection-to-injection
standard deviation. Calendar date is the current proxy for derivatization batch.

For each compound, let `C_AA` and `C_NACME` come from the `AA_mix` standard
metadata and `C_total = C_AA + C_NACME`. Estimate the empirical NACME term from
the known EA-IRMS value and the same-date AA mix mean:

$$
\delta_{NACME} =
\frac{C_{total}\bar{\delta}_{STD} - C_{AA}\delta_{known}}
     {C_{NACME}}.
$$

Propagate the STD-injection SD and known-value uncertainty using the benchmark convention:

$$
\sigma_{NACME} = 
\sqrt{
  \left(\frac{C_{total}}{C_{NACME}}\sigma_{STD}\right)^2 +
  \left(\frac{C_{AA}}{C_{NACME}}\sigma_{known}\right)^2
}
$$

For a sample peak with a same-date estimate, calculate:

$$
\delta_{AA,corr} =
\frac{C_{total}\delta_{sample} - C_{NACME}\delta_{NACME}}
     {C_{AA}}.
$$

Carry the empirical NACME estimate and its uncertainty as diagnostics; the
estimate absorbs differences between the known AA value and measured standard,
so it is not necessarily a physically interpretable reagent value. Preserve the
reference convention for uncertainty: use the SD of STD injections (not the SE
of their mean), combined with the known-value uncertainty. Exclude AA mix runs
from corrected sample output, leave corrections missing when no same-date
compound estimate exists, and leave unmatched or ambiguous peaks unassigned for
review. Resolve the AA mix sample label from the actual exports rather than
assuming it is literally named `STD`.

The synthetic regression benchmark in `tests/fixtures/DeltaCalculations_example.xlsx`
is checked by the `testthat` suite. It compares external and NACME correction
stages without treating the workbook as an instrument export. The AA mix label
is configurable because exports may label those injections differently from
the reference standard ID.
